scope: 18 completed observations: same buffered harness, interleaved before/after ReadIndex completion handoff; P1 uniform/hotspot and P2 eight clients.
metric: Median of three run values. Throughput counts successful logical confirmations inside the 180-second window; latency includes drain tails. Per-run percentiles are not pooled.
cost_method: Join each successful logical operation to its single C++ call. Outside-call mean is computed per request, not by subtracting percentiles. C++ call includes client/trace work, not just server time. Process counters use first/last samples inside Python window.
limitations: Original simplistic results use old file backend/toolchain and old harness; observed ratios are historical whole-system comparisons, not same-harness database speedups.
The before/after experiment isolates completion handoff, not ReadIndex numbering/grouping versus b709e0a.
Three adjacent pairs show direction and variation, not statistical proof of equivalence or causation of small differences.
P3, P4 and P2 four clients were not rerun; recovery and turnover pain points remain outside this round.
STATUS and storage observation failures during startup/teardown must not be counted as measured SQL failures.
findings: Both versions finish all 18 observations with successful business validation and cleanup. After: 881747 successful measured reads and 18246 committed measured writes, no raw business errors/retries/deadline misses. Nine after reads were skipped at the workload cutoff before execution.
The previous node binary with the new buffered harness already measures 810.86/827.25 P1 ops/s. The rise from historical 285.76/281.72 cannot be attributed to the new node handoff change.
Identical-harness handoff comparison: uniform +0.37%, hotspot -1.31%, P2 eight clients -0.31%. No consistent throughput benefit; hotspot is lower in each of the three adjacent pairs.

Python read-family syscalls fall from historical 91983143/89146204 to 284413/272824 per sampled P1 window, despite processing more requests. Outside-C++-call means fall from 10.91/11.70 ms to 1.26/1.97 ms. These are observer/client costs, not server phase measurements.
P2 paired differences have mixed signs (+2.42%, -0.31%, -1.54%). This does not prove the earlier ReadIndex package has no cost versus b709e0a; b709e0a was not rerun with the new harness.

P2 after still averages about 237.50 ms inside the client call versus 0.93 ms outside it, with about 7.96 of 8 calls in flight. Further write optimization needs phase attribution inside that call, not an assumption that buffered output or ReadIndex dominates.

P1 numeric comparisons exceed the original historic results by 23.60%/24.12%, but the original code was not rerun under the new harness. No same-harness claim of database-core speedup over the original is supported.
